edges.effect_quant: This is one of the clearest long-term protective signals in reproductive epidemiology. In a collaborative individual-participant meta-analysis of 110,560 women, each 5 years of oral-contraceptive use was linked to about a 29% lower ovarian-cancer risk when use had ceased within the prior decade, and benefit persisted for decades after stopping. Additional case-control and BRCA-carrier cohort data support the same direction.
edges.population: women using combined oral contraceptives, including general-population users and high-risk BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation carriers
edges.mechanism: Combined oral contraceptives suppress ovulation and reduce repeated epithelial disruption and repair at the ovarian surface. That lower lifetime ovulatory burden is the leading biologic explanation for the durable reduction in epithelial ovarian-cancer risk seen across observational datasets.
edges.summary: The ovarian-cancer signal is strongly protective and unusually consistent. Large pooled epidemiology, conventional case-control data, and hereditary-risk cohorts all point in the same direction: longer combined oral-contraceptive exposure is associated with lower ovarian-cancer risk, and the protection often persists long after discontinuation.
edges.caveats: Absolute benefit varies with baseline risk, duration of use, and tumor subtype, and mucinous tumors appear less affected than other epithelial subtypes. Any counseling still has to weigh this protection against other oral-contraceptive tradeoffs, including a small breast-cancer signal in current or recent users and a more mixed cervical-cancer literature.

evidence.citation: Collaborative Group on Epidemiological Studies of Ovarian Cancer 2008 Lancet
evidence.notes: Ovarian cancer and oral contraceptives: collaborative reanalysis of data from 45 epidemiological studies including 23,257 women with ovarian cancer and 87,303 controls.

effect_quant.comparator: ovarian-cancer risk per 5 years of combined oral-contraceptive use among women whose use had ceased less than 10 years earlier

evidence.notes: A case-control study of oral contraceptive use and invasive epithelial ovarian cancer.
